findings.title: include_website_name missing trailing question mark
findings.body: The new method `def include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?`. ActiveModel::Serializer's inclusion check probes for `include_<attr>?`; because the method is named `include_website_name` (no `?`), the serializer never calls it and `website_name` is unconditionally included in the JSON payload even when `website` is blank (where it ends up as a noisy `null`). It should be `def include_website_name?`. The rest of the file (and the `untrusted_attributes`/`private_attributes`/`staff_attributes` macros) consistently use the `include_<attr>?` form, confirming the expected convention.

findings.title: website_name leaks info that should be hidden for TL0 users
findings.body: `website_name` is added to the public `attributes` list but is not registered as an `untrusted_attribute` next to `:website`. `untrusted_attributes` is what hides fields from anonymous viewers looking at TL0 (new) users via `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. Because `website_name` is derived from `website` (it is exactly the host, and the path when domains match), hiding `website` while exposing `website_name` defeats the purpose of that filter: an anonymous visitor can still read `example.com/user` for any TL0 user. `:website_name` should be added to the `untrusted_attributes :bio_raw, :bio_cooked, :bio_excerpt, :location, :website, :profile_background, :card_background` list, and the matching spec assertion in `spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb` should be extended to assert `website_name` is absent for the TL0/anonymous context.

findings.title: URI(...).path drops query string and fragment
findings.body: `URI(...).path` returns only the path component, so any `?query` and `#fragment` parts of the user's stored website URL are silently discarded when building `website_name` (e.g. `http://example.com/user?ref=foo` becomes `example.com/user`). If the intent of the PR is to show the "complete URL path", `URI(...).request_uri` (or path + query + fragment) should be used so query parameters and anchors are preserved.

findings.title: URI(website.to_s) parsed multiple times
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed three separate times inside `website_name` (once for `host`, then again twice for `.path`). On a hot serializer called for every user payload, this is wasteful and harder to read. The URI object should be parsed once into a local variable and `host`/`path` (or `request_uri`) read from it.

findings.title: Missing coverage for several branches of website_name
findings.body: The new specs only exercise three cases (different 2-part host, identical host, subdomain/parent 3-part host). They do not cover: (a) the second branch where both hosts have the same number of parts greater than two (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) and a non-matching second-level label; (b) websites whose path includes a query string or fragment, to verify whether they are preserved or dropped; (c) websites with a non-default port; (d) websites whose scheme is missing or unparseable, to verify the `rescue nil` path doesn't leak garbage. None of these are covered by the existing TL0/untrusted test either, so the privacy regression on `:website_name` going through without `untrusted_attributes` is also untested.
